answer: In a mesa-mapping market, each agent identity is a vertex in the trading graph and must lock a fixed bond for 90 days before receiving one vote on map updates. Bonds cannot back multiple identities simultaneously, so hollow profiles alone confer no power. An attacker seeking 1,000 votes must lock 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and bearing its opportunity cost. This prices a sybil swarm rather than pretending to prove identities are unique.
